question: A new mother is talking to people who are not in the room and acting very confused. What should a midwife do first?

options.A: Assume she is just exhausted from a long labor and wait two days
options.B: Rule out physical medical emergencies like eclampsia or severe infection
options.C: Immediately discharge her home with a relative for close observation
options.D: Prescribe strong antipsychotic medications without consulting a doctor

explanation: Physical medical issues causing confusion must always be checked first to keep the mother safe. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T3#BMP223_U3_T3_h1)

question: How do most antidepressant medications reach the growing fetus during pregnancy?

options.A: By traveling upward from the maternal vagina
options.B: By direct absorption through the amniotic fluid
options.C: By synthesis within the fetal liver
options.D: By crossing the placental barrier

explanation: Antidepressants can easily pass through the placenta and enter the baby's bloodstream. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which type of emergency contraceptive pill is most commonly found in Nigerian pharmacies and clinics?

options.A: Progesterone blocking implants
options.B: Combined estrogen-only patches
options.C: Levonorgestrel-only pills
options.D: Ulipristal acetate tablets

explanation: Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg is widely distributed and easily accessible across health facilities and chemist shops in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T10#BMP224_U3_T10_h2)

question: What critical instruction must a midwife give a patient regarding their daily steroid tablets?

options.A: Never stop taking them abruptly without medical advice
options.B: Double the daily dose only when going on a long journey
options.C: Skip the morning dose if appetite is poor
options.D: Stop taking them immediately if a mild headache occurs

explanation: Abrupt cessation of corticosteroid replacement can quickly trigger a fatal Addisonian crisis. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T7#BMP216_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which visual aid is best for showing step-by-step storytelling during a community talk?

options.A: Written pamphlets
options.B: Flipcharts
options.C: Medical journals
options.D: Spreadsheet graphs

explanation: Flipcharts allow the health educator to turn pages sequentially, making them ideal for showing chronological processes like labor. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T2#BMP227_U2_T2_h3)

question: Where should the midwife place the first stitch when repairing a vaginal mucosal tear?

options.A: At the lower edge near the anal sphincter
options.B: Directly at the midpoint of the hymenal ring
options.C: About 1 centimeter above the apex of the wound
options.D: Right on the skin of the perineal body

explanation: Starting slightly above the apex ensures that any bleeding vessels hidden at the very top of the tear are securely tied off. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why do monochorionic twin pregnancies require more frequent ultrasound scans than dichorionic twin pregnancies?

options.A: Identical twins grow much faster and will outgrow the uterine cavity prematurely
options.B: Monochorionic placentas dissolve much earlier in the second trimester
options.C: The ultrasound machine cannot visualize dichorionic membranes clearly after 20 weeks
options.D: They carry a high risk of shared placental vascular complications that need early detection

explanation: Shared blood vessels in a single placenta can lead to dangerous imbalances like twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, requiring close observation. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T8#BMP311_U1_T8_h3)

question: What does it mean if the inner square of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) is darker than the outer circle?

options.A: The vaccine has frozen and formed ice crystals
options.B: The vaccine has suffered heat damage and must be discarded
options.C: The vaccine expiry date has been extended
options.D: The vaccine is brand new and has maximum potency

explanation: A darkened inner square indicates cumulative heat exposure that ruins the vaccine, meaning it cannot be administered. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the expected pattern of asthma symptom changes across a population of pregnant women?

options.A: Symptoms invariably worsen during the third trimester for every patient
options.B: Most patients experience sudden improvement once progesterone peaks
options.C: One-third improve, one-third worsen, and one-third stay the same
options.D: Nearly all women experience a complete remission of wheezing episodes

explanation: Clinical experience shows that asthma behavior during pregnancy follows a predictable split thirds rule. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T11#BMP221_U4_T11_h2)

question: What does the term 'child spacing' specifically mean in reproductive health?

options.A: The time period between one pregnancy and the next
options.B: The duration of exclusive breastfeeding for an infant
options.C: The age difference between the oldest and youngest child
options.D: The physical distance between maternity hospitals in a state

explanation: Child spacing measures the interval of time between a previous delivery and the start of a subsequent pregnancy. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T1#BMP224_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which common germ causes the vast majority of simple bladder infections?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation: Escherichia coli lives naturally in the bowel and is responsible for up to ninety percent of bladder infections caught in the community. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T3#BMP216_U1_T3_h2)

question: A facility submits its monthly NHMIS report late, on the twentieth day of the following month. What is the immediate consequence of this delay?

options.A: It automatically cancels all vaccine deliveries for the clinic.
options.B: It erases all electronic records stored on the server.
options.C: It requires the midwife in charge to pay a cash fine.
options.D: It holds up regional collation and delays national health planning.

explanation: Late facility reports break the timeline for LGA and state compilation, delaying the entire country's health data updates. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why do midwives prefer standardized screening tools over casual questioning about drug use?

options.A: They reduce personal bias and help patients feel less judged
options.B: They measure exact blood levels of substances instantly
options.C: They require a medical doctor to interpret every single answer
options.D: They automatically cure the addiction upon completion

explanation: Using validated questionnaires ensures every woman is asked the same neutral questions, which lowers provider bias. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T8#BMP223_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why does IMCI use symptom-based color-coded charts instead of waiting for lab test results?

options.A: To replace the need for physical examination by trained health workers
options.B: To prove that laboratory testing is entirely unnecessary in clinics
options.C: To reduce the paperwork required for clinic record books
options.D: To enable rapid life-saving treatment decisions in resource-limited settings

explanation: Many primary clinics lack functional labs, so IMCI uses physical signs to guide urgent action immediately. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a primary duty of a midwife when a client expresses fear about contraceptive side effects?

options.A: Prescribe heavy sedatives to calm the client's anxiety down
options.B: Scold the client for listening to unverified community gossip
options.C: Provide empathetic, evidence-based reassurance and correct information
options.D: Refuse to issue any contraceptives until the client stops asking questions

explanation: Midwives must listen to client concerns respectfully and offer accurate medical facts to dispel myths. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T1#BMP224_U1_T1_h6)

question: How can an individual midwife promote rights-based care despite difficult working conditions?

options.A: By charging extra consultation fees to cover hospital shortages
options.B: By practicing respectful maternity care and educating clients
options.C: By refusing to attend to patients from outside her ethnic group
options.D: By ignoring hospital protocols when working night shifts

explanation: Midwives make a huge difference simply by treating clients with respect and empowering them through health education. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main problem with using unclear instructions at an OSCE station door?

options.A: It makes the examination take twice as long
options.B: It prevents the use of standardized patients
options.C: It causes student panic and unfair grading
options.D: It forces examiners to grade without checklists

explanation: Unclear prompts test guessing ability rather than actual clinical competence, compromising the validity of the exam. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h4)

question: Which worm is most responsible for causing severe iron-deficiency anaemia through blood loss?

options.A: Hookworm
options.B: Whipworm
options.C: Pinworm
options.D: Ascaris

explanation: Hookworms attach to the wall of the gut and feed on the host's blood, making them a major cause of anaemia in pregnancy in endemic areas. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T7#BMP116_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of using closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: To reduce the number of staff members needed in the room
options.B: To satisfy hospital accreditation requirements for record keeping
options.C: To make sure the patient falls asleep during the procedure
options.D: To confirm that orders are heard, understood, and executed

explanation: Repeating instructions back eliminates misunderstandings caused by background noise or stress in the emergency room. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h3)

question: Who primarily provided organized care for the sick during the early religious era of nursing?

options.A: Trained hospital administrators
options.B: Religious orders and monasteries
options.C: University-certified physicians
options.D: Government medical boards

explanation: Early organized healthcare facilities were predominantly established and managed by religious institutions and monastic groups before formal secular nursing schools emerged. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T2#BMP110_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following describes intersectoral collaboration in primary health care?

options.A: Sharing medical supplies between federal and state hospitals
options.B: Partnering only with international private donor agencies
options.C: Collaborating exclusively among different nursing specialties
options.D: Working with other sectors like agriculture and education

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration involves cooperation between health and non-health sectors to address the root causes of ill health. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T8#BMP117_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the most important clinical consideration for a midwife before administering any drug to an expectant mother?

options.A: Waiting until the postnatal period to provide any treatment
options.B: Ensuring the drug is manufactured exclusively within Nigeria
options.C: Weighing the therapeutic benefits against potential risks to the foetus
options.D: Confirming that the patient has never taken a tablet before

explanation: Because drugs cross the placenta, midwives must carefully balance the clinical need of the mother against potential harm to the baby. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T1#BMP124_U1_T1_h5)

question: What physical sign indicates that a uterine perforation with peritonitis has likely occurred?

options.A: Painless swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Rigid, tender abdomen with guarding
options.C: Complete absence of any vaginal discharge
options.D: Elevated blood pressure and flushed skin

explanation: Peritonitis causes the abdominal wall muscles to become tight and rigid, accompanied by severe tenderness when touched. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is heparin generally avoided during acute obstetric DIC when bleeding is already widespread?

options.A: It causes severe allergic reactions in postpartum women
options.B: It prevents further clotting when the patient is already at high risk of hemorrhaging
options.C: It immediately destroys all remaining red blood cells in the circulation
options.D: It permanently stops the kidneys from producing urine

explanation: Since the patient is already bleeding uncontrollably from a lack of clotting factors, giving an anti-clotting medication like heparin would worsen the hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h6)

question: How does the suckling pattern change after the milk ejection reflex is triggered?

options.A: It becomes erratic and involves chewing movements on the areola
options.B: It shifts from rapid shallow sucks to deep, slower sucks with pauses
options.C: It stops completely until the mother expresses milk manually
options.D: It speeds up into continuous rapid sucking without any pauses

explanation: Initial fast sucks stimulate milk flow, and once milk ejects, the baby changes to deep sucks with swallowing pauses to ingest milk efficiently. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T2#BMP214_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the most common reason clients stop taking progestin-only pills?

options.A: Severe permanent weight gain
options.B: Complete loss of appetite
options.C: Sudden and permanent hair loss
options.D: Changes in menstrual bleeding patterns

explanation: Irregular spotting or unpredictable bleeding often surprises clients who were not properly counseled, leading to discontinuation. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T5#BMP224_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the typical state of the external cervical os during a speculum examination for a complete abortion?

options.A: Bulging
options.B: Closed
options.C: Rigid
options.D: Wide open

explanation: Once all pregnancy tissue has passed and the uterus contracts, the cervix closes back up. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h2)

question: What does the letter 'E' stand for in the REEDA scale used by midwives to assess surgical incisions and perineal tears?

options.A: Edema
options.B: Electrolyte
options.C: Exudate
options.D: Erythrocyte

explanation: In the REEDA assessment tool, E stands for edema, which measures the amount of swelling present around a wound or repair. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T5#BMP111_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the main function of a secondary literature source?

options.A: To register a new clinical trial before data collection begins
options.B: To provide raw participant interview transcripts for public use
options.C: To record daily vital signs in a hospital maternity ward
options.D: To summarize and interpret multiple primary research studies

explanation: Secondary sources bring together various primary studies to give a broad overview of a clinical topic. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T1#BMP225_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why are the ovaries considered both exocrine and endocrine organs?

options.A: They produce digestive enzymes alongside monthly menstrual blood flow
options.B: They filter waste products from the pelvis while storing urine temporarily
options.C: They control both voluntary leg movements and involuntary uterine contractions
options.D: They release egg cells and also secrete reproductive hormones into the bloodstream

explanation: Ovaries produce gametes (ova) and secrete key hormones like estrogen and progesterone directly into the blood supply. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T2#BMP210_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which hormonal change immediately following childbirth contributes to chemical shifts linked to mood disorders?

options.A: Sharp drop in estrogen and progesterone
options.B: Permanent elevation of human placental lactogen
options.C: Sudden increase in placental growth hormone
options.D: Total cessation of thyroid hormone production

explanation: The rapid withdrawal of pregnancy hormones immediately after delivery is a primary biological trigger for mood instability. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T2#BMP223_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why must antivenom be given in a clinic or hospital equipped to handle severe reactions?

options.A: The medication must be boiled before entering the bloodstream.
options.B: Antivenom itself can trigger severe allergic reactions or anaphylaxis.
options.C: Hospital staff are the only people legally allowed to open the vial.
options.D: Patients always lose consciousness immediately upon receiving the injection.

explanation: Because antivenom is made from animal proteins, it can sometimes cause a severe allergic reaction that needs quick medical treatment. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h6)

question: Why does a midwife use a penlight to check a patient's mouth?

options.A: To measure the internal temperature of the mouth
options.B: To test the patient's vision and nerve function
options.C: To check the size, depth, and location of any mouth sores
options.D: To help produce saliva before taking a blood sample

explanation: Using a light allows the midwife to clearly see and record the exact features and spread of ulcers in the mouth. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T2#BMP125_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why are viruses called obligate intracellular parasites?

options.A: They survive easily outside living tissue
options.B: They multiply strictly by splitting in half
options.C: They possess their own complete metabolic system
options.D: They need host cell machinery to reproduce

explanation: Viruses cannot generate energy or build proteins on their own, so they must invade living host cells to multiply. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T9#BMP124_U4_T9_h1)

question: What is a major risk of giving systemic opioid pain relief to a woman who is very close to giving birth?

options.A: Complete stoppage of breast milk
options.B: Sudden high blood pressure spikes
options.C: Neonatal respiratory depression
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the legs

explanation: Opioids cross the placenta. If birth happens shortly after the injection, the newborn may have trouble breathing on its own. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T5#BMP212_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main effect of a sedative drug?

options.A: Triggers immediate deep surgical anesthesia
options.B: Increases heart rate and blood pressure
options.C: Calms anxiety and reduces motor activity
options.D: Stimulates the central nervous system

explanation: Sedatives are given to reduce anxiety and calm a patient without forcing them to sleep. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h1)

question: What facial appearance is classically seen in an infant with marasmus?

options.A: Old man face with sunken cheeks
options.B: Moon face with a rounded jaw
options.C: Swollen face with tight eyelids
options.D: Asymmetrical facial paralysis

explanation: The loss of facial fat pads creates a shrunken, wrinkled appearance often referred to as an old man's face. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T3#BMP118_U4_T3_h3)

question: Who typically selects the individuals who serve as Village Health Workers?

options.A: The state commissioner for health
options.B: International donor agencies
options.C: The local community members themselves
options.D: Federal hospital medical directors

explanation: Village Health Workers are chosen directly by their own community members to ensure trust and acceptance. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the single most frequent cause of cracked nipples during breastfeeding?

options.A: Incorrect positioning and poor attachment
options.B: Drinking too much warm water
options.C: Producing too much foremilk
options.D: Wearing a cotton nursing bra

explanation: A shallow latch puts direct pressure and friction on the nipple tip, which quickly breaks down the skin. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T5#BMP214_U3_T5_h2)

question: In a legal case about patient care, how do the courts view a client's medical chart?

options.A: The property of the attending doctor only
options.B: Merely an optional suggestion
options.C: Primary legal evidence of care
options.D: A temporary scrap paper document

explanation: Clinical records carry high legal weight and are reviewed by courts to see if proper midwifery care was given. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of these actions breaks patient confidentiality in a maternity ward?

options.A: Discussing a patient's delivery complications in the public corridor
options.B: Writing vital signs in the official labour register
options.C: Asking the doctor to review a high-risk antenatal chart
options.D: Handing over patient notes to the incoming shift midwife

explanation: Talking about private health matters where visitors or other patients can overhear violates confidentiality rules. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following conditions means nifedipine should not be given?

options.A: Baseline low blood pressure
options.B: Mild gestational diabetes
options.C: Mild pregnancy-related nausea
options.D: A history of large babies

explanation: Giving a blood pressure-lowering medication to a mother who already has low blood pressure is unsafe. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T5#BMP213_U1_T5_h6)

question: What common side effect should the midwife warn the client to expect immediately after copper IUCD insertion?

options.A: Permanent loss of bladder control
options.B: Sudden weight gain and facial swelling
options.C: Mild cramping and irregular spotting
options.D: Complete cessation of all monthly periods

explanation: Mild uterine cramping and light spotting are common responses immediately following an IUCD insertion. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T11#BMP224_U3_T11_h6)

question: What type of data is represented by numbers like birth weight in clinical research?

options.A: Theoretical data
options.B: Quantitative data
options.C: Descriptive text
options.D: Qualitative data

explanation: Numbers and measurements collected in a study are classified as quantitative data. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary reason for monitoring intravenous access sites very closely during long-term antibiotic therapy?

options.A: To prevent the development of secondary bacterial infections
options.B: To make sure the patient's blood pressure stays elevated
options.C: To measure the exact amount of urine produced each hour
options.D: To check if the patient is allergic to the plastic tubing

explanation: Long-term IV lines carry a risk of letting new germs enter the bloodstream, which can worsen the patient's infection or cause new complications. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T7#BMP125_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why should a midwife avoid massaging the injection site after giving standard DMPA?

options.A: It causes immediate severe muscle necrosis
options.B: It neutralizes the active progestin ingredient
options.C: It forces the medication back out through the skin hole
options.D: It can speed up drug absorption and alter hormone levels

explanation: Massaging an intramuscular depot injection changes how fast the drug is released into the bloodstream, which is not recommended. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T6#BMP224_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for straining a patient's urine during an episode of renal colic?

options.A: To prevent the patient from developing a urinary tract infection
options.B: To remove dangerous blood clots blocking the urinary catheter
options.C: To catch passed stone fragments for laboratory analysis
options.D: To measure the exact total volume of urine produced each hour

explanation: Straining the urine allows the healthcare team to retrieve the stone so its chemical composition can be tested in the lab. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T10#BMP216_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is a common psychological challenge experienced by women admitted for long periods in high-risk wards?

options.A: Sudden loss of all long-term memory function
options.B: Anxiety, depression, and emotional fatigue
options.C: Complete indifference to their own health status
options.D: Aggressive hostility toward all newborn babies

explanation: Being away from home, family, and normal routines while worrying about pregnancy outcomes takes a heavy emotional toll. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h7)

question: Which of these routine vaccines is matched with the correct administration route?

options.A: Measles vaccine given orally as liquid drops
options.B: BCG vaccine given subcutaneously in the buttocks
options.C: Oral Polio Vaccine given via deep intramuscular injection
options.D: Pentavalent vaccine given intramuscularly in the mid-thigh

explanation: Pentavalent vaccine is an intramuscular injection administered into the anterolateral thigh of infants. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T3#BMP117_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which harmful practice do some mothers mistakenly try when their child develops acute watery diarrhea?

options.A: Giving frequent small sips of ORS from a clean cup
options.B: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.C: Giving the correct dose of zinc tablets daily
options.D: Withholding food to let the child's stomach rest

explanation: Starving a sick child is a dangerous misconception that worsens nutritional status and delays gut healing. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T3#BMP222_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is patient autonomy particularly important when providing antenatal and maternity care?

options.A: Pregnant women possess advanced medical degrees prior to admission
options.B: Women have the right to make informed choices regarding their own bodies and health
options.C: Hospital management requires written consent forms for statistical records
options.D: Midwives are legally absolved of all responsibility if a patient refuses treatment

explanation: Autonomy ensures that healthcare respects individual dignity by allowing mothers to participate actively in decisions affecting their pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h3)

question: A midwife receives conflicting instructions about patient triage from both the matron and the shift coordinator. Which of Fayol's principles is being broken?

options.A: Remuneration
options.B: Unity of command
options.C: Esprit de corps
options.D: Scalar chain

explanation: When staff receive competing orders from multiple leaders, the principle of unity of command is broken, leading to workplace confusion. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T2#BMP312_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for small or vulnerable babies?

options.A: To allow the mother to sleep uninterrupted through the night
options.B: To completely replace the need for expressed breast milk feeds
options.C: To speed up the infant's discharge from the hospital within 24 hours
options.D: To stabilize temperature, heart rate, and encourage feeding readiness

explanation: KMC uses skin-to-skin contact to keep tiny newborns warm and stable while helping them grow and get ready to breastfeed. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h4)

question: If a woman has a roomy gynecoid pelvis, what does this mean for the baby during labour?

options.A: The baby's head will remain unengaged until pushing begins
options.B: The baby will experience immediate shoulder dystocia at the inlet
options.C: The baby will find it easy to turn its head inside the pelvis
options.D: The baby is forced to stay in a breech position

explanation: A roomy mid-pelvis with good side-to-side space supports smooth internal rotation of the baby's head during the second stage of labour. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T3#BMP210_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main idea behind the Germ Theory of Disease?

options.A: Body fluid imbalances cause most bacterial infections
options.B: Bad air is the primary source of all human fever
options.C: Specific micro-organisms cause specific infectious illnesses
options.D: Viruses can transform into bacteria inside wounds

explanation: The germ theory states that specific microscopic pathogens are responsible for specific diseases. [learn more](BMP116_U1_T1#BMP116_U1_T1_h3)

question: How do progestin-only pills primarily block sperm from reaching an egg?

options.A: Immediate neutralization of vaginal pH levels
options.B: Thickening of the cervical mucus
options.C: Induction of rapid uterine muscle contractions
options.D: Complete destruction of all active sperm in the vagina

explanation: Progestin alters cervical secretions, making them too thick for sperm to swim through and reach the egg. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T5#BMP224_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the water seal chamber in a chest drainage system?

options.A: To measure total daily blood loss from the patient
options.B: To dilute thick pus or blood coming from the chest
options.C: To provide active mechanical suctioning to the lung tissue
options.D: To act as a one-way valve preventing air from entering the chest

explanation: The water seal lets air escape from the patient during expiration while blocking room air from rushing back in during inspiration. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T11#BMP125_U1_T11_h3)

question: What should be your main priority during a severe staff shortage on a maternity ward?

options.A: Deep cleaning the empty rooms on the private wing
options.B: Conducting long lectures for junior student nurses
options.C: Immediate life-saving clinical care for unstable patients
options.D: Filing all routine monthly administrative paperwork

explanation: When resources are stretched thin, preserving patient survival takes precedence over clerical duties. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h6)

question: A student wants to study every health issue affecting pregnant women across the entire country. What is the main problem with this topic?

options.A: It is far too broad and lacks feasibility for a single researcher
options.B: It focuses on an uninteresting topic with no clinical relevance
options.C: It is completely unethical and poses physical danger to patients
options.D: It is too narrow and has already been answered definitively

explanation: Broad topics covering massive populations and regions are unmanageable and lack feasibility, requiring narrowing down. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T10#BMP225_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why does cervical mucus change its consistency across the menstrual cycle?

options.A: Vaginal pH drops sharply during the menstrual bleeding phase
options.B: Shifting hormone levels alter the fluid secreted by the cervix
options.C: Bacterial flora in the vagina multiply rapidly after ovulation
options.D: Dietary changes directly modify reproductive tract secretions

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone control the type of mucus the cervix produces at different times of the cycle. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h4)

question: What happens when a Clostridium spore finds a warm, nutrient-rich place with no oxygen?

options.A: It turns into a harmless plant seed
options.B: It stops producing all harmful toxins
options.C: It turns into an active cell
options.D: It immediately dissolves into water

explanation: Favorable conditions trigger the dormant spore to transform back into a growing bacterial cell capable of producing toxins. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T8#BMP116_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main difference between copying a file and moving a file?

options.A: Copying changes the file format, whereas moving keeps the format the same
options.B: Copying permanently deletes the file, whereas moving saves it to a flash drive
options.C: Copying leaves the original file in place while creating a duplicate, whereas moving relocates it entirely
